answers.question: Why microservices for GenieA, and why split them across FastAPI, NestJS and Go?
answers.answer: Each part of GenieA can scale, fail and deploy on its own. If AI or SMS goes down, SOS and live tracking keep running. Three stacks: each service uses the right tool for its job: NestJS for business and admin logic (auth, cases, tenants). FastAPI for AI and location, because Python has the best libraries for both. Go for realtime chat and calls and for notifications, because it handles many open connections cheaply.

answers.question: Your worst production incident: what broke, how you found it, what you changed afterwards.
How do you take an ML feature (like the RAG pipeline or the voice assistant) from prototype to something reliable?
answers.answer: I treat a model like any other backend service: it sits behind an API with a clear contract, so the apps never talk to it directly. At Star Technologies the RAG pipeline (retrieval over vector search) and the voice assistant both ship as backend APIs, monitored with Prometheus, Grafana and CloudWatch like the rest of production. At Megamind it was the same idea offline: fine-tuned, quantized models served behind REST inference APIs.
